title: Agree the auto fare before you sit
body: Most autos in Jaipur don't run on the meter. Say where you're going, ask 'Kitna lagega?', and agree a number before you get in. If it feels high, smile, say no thanks, and wave down the next one. There's always a next one.

title: Book autos on an app
body: Ride-hailing apps offer autos in Jaipur at a fixed fare shown upfront. Great for short hops in the old city and no bargaining needed. Keep some small cash: some drivers prefer it.

title: App cabs for longer rides
body: For Amer, Sanganer or the airport, app cabs are comfortable and fairly priced. Share the exact pin, not just the area name. Check the number plate matches before you get in.

title: Hiring a driver for the day
body: For Amer plus Jaigarh, or the Abhaneri day trip, a cab for the day makes sense. Agree the hours, kilometres and stops in writing (WhatsApp is fine). Say clearly at the start: 'No shopping stops, please.'

title: Walk the old-city bazaars
body: Johari, Bapu and Tripolia Bazaar are best on foot. The arcades give shade, and many shops sit just inside side lanes. Wear shoes you can step around puddles in, and keep your bag in front in crowds.

title: Crossing the road, Jaipur style
body: Traffic rarely stops, but it does flow around you. Cross at a steady pace, don't run or freeze, and when in doubt cross alongside a local. Watch for scooters coming the wrong way.

title: Amer first thing in the morning
body: Get to Amber Fort right when it opens. You'll beat the heat and the tour buses, and the light on the walls is lovely. Pair it with Panna Meena ka Kund and Jaigarh, then head back for lunch.

title: When to hit the markets
body: Many old-city shops open late morning, around 10:30 or 11, and stay open into the evening. Late afternoon to dusk is lively and cooler. Some shops or whole bazaars close one day a week, often Sunday, so check the listing before you go.

title: What to wear
body: Light, loose cotton that covers shoulders and knees is comfortable and respectful, especially at temples. Carry a scarf for sun and dust. Comfortable shoes beat pretty ones: forts mean ramps, steps and cobbles.

title: The friendly commission shop
body: If a driver or a stranger insists on taking you to a 'government emporium', a 'cousin's factory' or a 'special sale today', it's usually a commission shop, and the commission goes on your bill. Say you already have a list. Then go to the shop you chose.

title: Staying safe
body: Jaipur is generally friendly to travellers. Use normal city sense: keep your phone and wallet zipped, share your live location if you're out late, and use app cabs at night. If someone follows you or won't take no, walk into a busy shop and ask for help.

title: Heat and water
body: Even in winter, the afternoon sun is strong. Drink sealed bottled or filtered water, refill often, and take shade breaks. In summer, plan sightseeing for early morning and evening and rest in the afternoon.

title: Cash and UPI
body: UPI (pay by QR code) works almost everywhere, from big shops to chai stalls. Foreign cards don't always work for UPI, so carry some small notes for autos, stalls and tips. Ask for a bill for anything expensive.
